main_text.p: test.Morbi igitur,cùm accidentia sint,corporibus, utsuis proprijs subiectis dútaxat inhærent.Propterea Galenus libro Metho di nono,affectum omnem prꝑter naturā in similaribus partibus cósistere, aut in dissimilaribus scriptum nobis reliquit:Sententiæ cuius ipse Fernelius accedit: qui libro Methodi medendi primo, & de Differentijs morborum omnem morbum in corporis partisue substantia consistere apertissimè declarat. Quare Fernelius non sibi sem per satis constare uidetur. Adhæc si in partis similaris temperamento sita esset intem peries, reuera in eodem subiecto,corpore similari,duæ simul adessent qualitates contrariæ,nempe sanitas & morbus, seu affectus unus naturalis, & alter contra naturā. Similaris enim partis temperamentum sanitatem esse, & intemperiem huic oppositam,morbum, ne medicos quidè, eos, qui mediocriter in medicina uersati sunt, latere putamus.Nihil namq; aliud est intempe ries, quàm mutata corporis temperies, & qualitatum symmetria: unde unum pellere alterum(contrariorum instar) necesse est.

page.notes: The closing word "EX-" at the lower right is a catchword, not text: it is the first word of the next page and is recorded here only. Printing errors left as printed: "test.Morbi", "dútaxat", "semper" read as "sem per" in the print. Some words in the first lines are set in a slightly blurred impression; "subiectis" and "substantia" are read as printed with [?] omitted because they are clear.
